hypothesis: Five individual Michigan beach pages already rank on page one but their search-facing openings under-answer local conditions, water-quality and posted-flag intent. Query-specific titles, H1s and direct first answers should convert existing visibility into clicks while the statewide Beach Report root remains unchanged.

measurement.windowStarts: first complete America/Detroit day after production release
measurement.primaryMetric: aggregate and page-level Search Console CTR
measurement.decisionRule: Keep the treatment if aggregate CTR materially improves while the five-page weighted average position remains at or better than 10.5. Evaluate page-level outliers separately rather than reverting the whole cluster for one weak page.

truthBoundary: Never claim a physical posted beach flag is known remotely or that BeachGuard or NWS data certifies a beach safe to swim. Posted signs, flags, lifeguards, official closures and onsite conditions remain authoritative.
rootGuardrail: Do not change /great-lakes-beaches/ while its statewide Beach Conditions CTR experiment is protected.
releaseDateModifiedNote: The dateModified every treated page must carry. Was hardcoded as 2026-08-22 in the benchmark script, which broke the moment the stamper told the truth about a later content change. Keep it here so the pin and the config cannot disagree. Bump it whenever the treatment re-ships before its window opens; do not bump it once status is running.

latestObserved.interpretation: Aggregate CTR and weighted position improved versus baseline. New Buffalo is above the experiment CTR target; Warren Dunes and P.J. Hoffmaster are the highest-impression laggards. Preserve the five-page freeze and evaluate those outliers separately after a clean measurement window rather than resetting the whole cluster.

measurementDecision.reason: The experiment is improving overall and summer beach demand is rolling off after September 15. Search-facing changes now would confound the treatment and seasonal interpretation.
